feed.text:
Nobody is coming to save you.

My rule for this week: decide who you are before the week decides for you. Epictetus was born a slave and still told his students, in Discourses 3.23, "First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do." Say it, then do it. Every day.

Save this. Start Monday.

#stoicism #epictetus #purpose #youngmen #discipline #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 11.7: "How clearly it strikes you that there is no other condition of life so well adapted for the practice of philosophy as this one in which you now find yourself."

One word: who do you want to be by Friday? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Nobody is coming to save you. Epictetus, Discourses 3.23.

feed.text:
Your mind is turning into what you scroll.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 5.16: "The soul becomes dyed with the colour of its thoughts." My rule: whatever goes in on repeat becomes you. Rage bait makes an angry man, comparison makes a small one, good books make a good one. Pick the dye.

Follow for one rule a day.

#stoicism #marcusaurelius #mindset #youngmen #selfimprovement #stoic #philosophy #dailystoic
feed.first:
Epictetus, Discourses 2.18: "Every habit and faculty is confirmed and grows by the corresponding actions."

What's the last thing you read that actually made you better? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Your mind is turning into what you scroll. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 5.16.

feed.text:
You can survive anything with one thing.

Nietzsche wrote it in Twilight of the Idols: "He who has a why to live can bear almost any how." Viktor Frankl quoted it in the camps and watched it hold true. My rule: when the how gets heavy, go back to the why. If you don't have one yet, finding it is the job.

Send this to someone carrying a lot.

#stoicism #nietzsche #viktorfrankl #purpose #suffering #youngmen #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Frankl again, Man's Search for Meaning: "Those who have a 'why' to live, can bear with almost any 'how'." He saw it with his own eyes.

What's your why right now, in a few words? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how. Nietzsche, Twilight of the Idols.

feed.text:
Tired. Broke. Nobody watching. Doesn't change the job.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 6.2: "Just that you do the right thing. The rest doesn't matter. Cold or warm. Tired or well-rested. Despised or honoured." My rule: the conditions are never going to be right. Do it anyway.

Save this for the days you want to quit.

#stoicism #marcusaurelius #discipline #virtue #youngmen #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Epictetus, Enchiridion 50: "Whatever rules you have adopted, abide by them as laws, and as if you would be impious to transgress them."

What's the one right thing you keep postponing because the timing is off? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Just that you do the right thing. The rest doesn't matter. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 6.2.

feed.text:
Three days. For a stranger. 😅

Epictetus, Enchiridion 5: "Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things." My rule: the comment didn't hurt you. Your opinion of the comment did. Close the app, go lift something.

Tag the friend who's still typing.

#stoicmemes #epictetus #philosophymemes #youngmen #stoicism #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 9.42: "When you run up against someone else's shamelessness, ask yourself: is a world without shamelessness possible? No. Then don't ask the impossible."

Longest you've ever stewed over a comment? Hours, days or weeks? 👇
feed.alt: Text meme. Me: loses one argument with a stranger online, thinks about the perfect comeback for three days. Epictetus: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things. Enchiridion 5.

feed.text:
Anyone can get angry. That's easy.

Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics II.9: "To be angry with the right person, to the right degree, at the right time, for the right purpose, and in the right way: that is not easy." My rule: anger isn't a sin, it's a tool. Most men swing it at the wrong target. Aim.

Send this to a brother with a short fuse.

#aristotle #anger #selfcontrol #youngmen #stoicism #virtue #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Seneca, On Anger 1.1: "No plague has cost the human race more."

Who actually deserved your anger last week, and who just got it? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Anyone can get angry. Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics II.9.

feed.text:
You don't want responsibility? Someone worse will take it.

Plato, Republic Book I: "The heaviest penalty for declining to rule is to be ruled by someone inferior to yourself." My rule: the team, the family, your own life. Lead it or watch someone less careful lead it for you.

Follow for more.

#plato #leadership #purpose #youngmen #stoicism #responsibility #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 6.30: "Fight to be the man philosophy wanted to make you."

Where in your life have you been waiting for someone else to take charge? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: The heaviest penalty for declining to rule. Plato, Republic Book I.

feed.text:
Everything hit you at once this week.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 4.49: "Be like the headland on which the waves break. It stands firm, and the seething waters around it fall asleep." My rule: you don't have to beat the storm. You have to still be standing when it's over.

Save this for the next storm.

#stoicism #marcusaurelius #suffering #resilience #youngmen #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Seneca, Letter 78: "Nothing is so hard that the mind cannot overcome it, provided it resolves to conquer."

What's the wave you're standing in right now? One word is enough. 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Be like the headland on which the waves break. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 4.49.

feed.text:
Everything that happens to you has two handles.

Epictetus, Enchiridion 43: "Every thing has two handles, one by which it may be carried, the other by which it cannot." His example was a brother who wrongs you: carry it by 'he's my brother', not by 'he wronged me'. My rule: before you react, check which handle you're holding.

Send this to someone holding a grudge.

#epictetus #stoicism #forgiveness #family #youngmen #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 10.4: "If he's making a mistake, correct him gently and show him where he went wrong. If you can't do that, then the blame lies with you."

Who in your life are you carrying by the wrong handle? Just the role, no names. 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Every thing has two handles. Epictetus, Enchiridion 43.

feed.text:
You can fight your life or you can walk with it.

Seneca, Letter 107, quoting the old Stoic Cleanthes: "Fate leads the willing and drags the unwilling." My rule: amor fati isn't giving up. It's refusing to be dragged. Same road either way. Walk it standing.

Save this.

#amorfati #seneca #stoicism #youngmen #purpose #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Epictetus, Enchiridion 53, the same prayer: "Lead me, Zeus, and you, Fate, wherever you have assigned me. I will follow without hesitation."

What's one thing in your life you've stopped fighting and started walking with? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Fate leads the willing and drags the unwilling. Seneca, Letter 107.

feed.text:
They can take everything from you. Except one thing.

Viktor Frankl, Man's Search for Meaning: "Everything can be taken from a man but one thing: the last of the human freedoms, to choose one's attitude in any given set of circumstances." He wrote it after Auschwitz. My rule: your situation is not your decision. Your response is.

Send this to someone who feels trapped.

#viktorfrankl #suffering #meaning #youngmen #stoicism #mindset #resilience #dailystoic
feed.first:
Epictetus, Discourses 1.1: "They can fetter my leg, but not even Zeus can conquer my will."

What's one situation you can't change this month, where you can still choose the attitude? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: The last of the human freedoms. Viktor Frankl, Man's Search for Meaning.

feed.text:
Asking for help isn't weak.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.7: "Do not be ashamed to be helped. Like a soldier storming a wall, you have a job to do. What if you are lame and cannot climb alone, but could with someone's help?" The emperor of Rome. My rule: the mission matters more than your pride. Lean on someone, then keep climbing.

Send this to a brother who's struggling in silence.

#stoicism #marcusaurelius #mentalhealth #youngmen #brotherhood #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Seneca, Letter 109: "The wise man needs hands, eyes, and many things that are necessary for his daily use." Even the wise man.

Who's one person you could text today for help you've been avoiding asking for? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Do not be ashamed to be helped. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.7.

feed.text:
You don't need a holiday. You need this.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 4.3: "Nowhere can a man find a quieter or more untroubled retreat than in his own soul." My rule: ten quiet minutes, no phone, once a day. It's free, it's always open, and it's the one place nobody can follow you into.

Save this for when it gets loud.

#stoicism #marcusaurelius #peace #beauty #youngmen #mindfulness #stoic #dailystoic
feed.first:
Seneca, Letter 28: "You need a change of soul rather than a change of climate."

When was the last time you sat for ten minutes with nothing? Be honest. 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Nowhere can a man find a quieter retreat than in his own soul. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 4.3.

feed.text:
You're afraid your life will be short.

Seneca, Letter 77: "As with a play, so with life: what matters is not how long it is, but how well it is acted." My rule: stop counting years. Count honest days. A short life lived fully beats a long one on autopilot.

Follow for one rule a day.

#seneca #stoicism #purpose #mementomori #youngmen #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 4.17: "Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. While you live, while it is in your power, be good."

If today were the last scene, did you act it well? Yes or not yet. 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: As with a play, so with life. Seneca, Letter 77.

feed.text:
They got away with it. You didn't.

Plato, Gorgias 469c, Socrates speaking: "It is worse to do wrong than to suffer wrong." My rule: the man who cheated you has to live inside the man who cheats. You don't. Staying clean is the win, even when it doesn't feel like one.

Send this to someone who got burned.

#plato #socrates #virtue #justice #youngmen #stoicism #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 9.4: "Whoever does wrong, wrongs himself."

Have you ever been glad, later, that you didn't get even? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: It is worse to do wrong than to suffer wrong. Plato, Gorgias 469c.

feed.text:
Injured. Sick. Broke. Still you.

Epictetus, Enchiridion 9: "Sickness is a hindrance to the body, but not to the will, unless the will itself chooses." He walked with a limp his whole life. My rule: when the body or the bank account is down, the character stays on duty.

Save this for the hard days.

#epictetus #stoicism #suffering #resilience #youngmen #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Seneca, Letter 78, written from his own sickbed: "Besides, what you can do in the sick room is to be an example."

What's one thing your body or your situation can't stop you from doing today? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Sickness is a hindrance to the body, but not to the will. Epictetus, Enchiridion 9.

feed.text:
You want the whole life fixed by Friday.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 8.32: "Build your life action by action, and be content if each one achieves its goal as far as it can." My rule: nobody builds a man in a weekend. One honest action, then the next, and in a year you won't recognise yourself.

Follow for more.

#stoicism #marcusaurelius #purpose #discipline #youngmen #selfimprovement #stoic #dailystoic
feed.first:
Epictetus, Discourses 1.15: "Nothing great is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig."

What's the one action you'll take today, not plan, take? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Build your life action by action. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 8.32.

feed.text:
You didn't choose your family. Or your city. Or your time.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 6.39: "Love the people fate has brought you together with, and do it with all your heart." He didn't choose his either. My rule: amor fati starts with the people in your kitchen. Stop wishing for a different hand. Play this one with love.

Send this to the people you're stuck with.

#amorfati #marcusaurelius #family #stoicism #youngmen #love #stoic #dailystoic
feed.first:
Seneca, Letter 9: "The wise man wants friends, not that he may live happily, but in order to practise friendship."

Who's one person you've been given rather than chosen, and what's one good thing about them? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Love the people fate has brought you together with. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 6.39.

feed.text:
Something went wrong today. Good.

Epictetus, Enchiridion 10: "On every accident that befalls you, remember to turn to yourself and ask what power you have for turning it to use." Insulted? Patience. Pain? Endurance. Loss? Freedom. My rule: every bad day is a drill. Run it.

Save this for the next bad day.

#epictetus #stoicism #amorfati #resilience #youngmen #stoic #mindset #dailystoic
feed.first:
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 8.35: "The mind turns every obstacle into fuel, the way fire takes what is thrown on it and burns brighter."

What went wrong this week that you can turn to use? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Ask what power you have for turning it to use. Epictetus, Enchiridion 10.

feed.text:
You're looking for it everywhere but here.

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.59: "Dig within. Within is the wellspring of good, and it will always flow if you keep digging." My rule: the good man you want to become isn't in a course, a city or a girl. He's a decision, and you can make it today.

Follow for one rule a day.

#stoicism #marcusaurelius #virtue #beauty #youngmen #selfimprovement #stoic #dailystoic
feed.first:
Plato, Phaedrus, Socrates' prayer: "Give me beauty in the inward soul; and may the outward and inward man be at one."

What's one good thing in you that you've been underusing? 👇
feed.alt: Text reel: Dig within. Within is the wellspring of good. Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.59.

feed.text:
5 ancient lines for when life gets heavy.

Seneca, Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, Nietzsche and Viktor Frankl on what suffering is for. My rule for next week: stop asking "why me" and start asking "what is this making me". Swipe, pick one, and carry it into Monday.

Save this. Send it to a brother who's going through it.

#suffering #stoicism #youngmen #meaning #viktorfrankl #nietzsche #marcusaurelius #dailystoic
feed.first:
One more, Seneca, On Providence 2: "Without an adversary, prowess shrivels."

Which of the five do you need this week? Just the number. 👇
feed.alt: Carousel: 5 ancient lines for when life gets heavy. Seneca, Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, Nietzsche, Frankl.
